title: Three-Card Climb Lab: A Choice/Strategy Playground Where the Choice Space Is a Dial
subtitle: Pick 1 card per round; your stats auto-resolve against a guardian that grows each round. Sliders expose the choice space itself as the difficulty dial.

cover.alt: Three-Card Climb Lab: A Choice/Strategy Playground Where the Choice Space Is a Dial

coverWide.alt: Three-Card Climb Lab: A Choice/Strategy Playground Where the Choice Space Is a Dial

corePoints: Choice space as difficulty: 2/3/4 cards per round, adjustable
Risk accumulation: enemy growth slope adjustable from 0.6 to 2.0
Opportunity cost: pick 1 card and the rest are lost, consequences land on your stats immediately
Explainable outcomes: the damage formula is printed on the canvas and every combat report line is traceable
Economy is stored blood: every 10 gold auto-converts to 3 HP at camp

breakdown.title: Rule Skeleton
bullets: Each round, pick 1 of N cards (N = 2/3/4, adjustable): Attack +X / Shield +X / Economy +X; the rest are discarded
Combat auto-resolves after the pick: hits to kill = ceil(foe HP / your ATK); damage taken = (hits − 1) × max(1, foe ATK − your DEF)
Lose when HP hits 0; win by surviving round 12; final score = 300 + gold + remaining HP

breakdown.title: Behavior Loop
bullets: Read the board (your stats + current and next guardian preview) → deal cards (ATK 35% / DEF 30% / Economy 35%) → pick 1
Auto-resolve → +3 gold kill bounty → camp: every 10 gold auto-converts to 3 HP (heals only what is missing, cap 30)
The enemy grows with the slope every round (HP ≈ 3 + round × slope × 2.2, ATK ≈ 1 + round × slope × 0.8); back to reading the board

breakdown.title: Implementation Notes
bullets: Pure static single-file demo on the AtomCore engine: Canvas 2D, portrait 2:3, zero dependencies, zero external requests
Only two round phases, choose / resolve; a 550ms timer advances the round, guarded by a token against stale timers after restart
Two sliders (enemy growth slope / cards per round) take effect live via game.params in dealing and enemy generation
